parts.label: (a)
parts.text: With reference to thermal energy, state what is meant by two objects being in thermal equilibrium.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Two cylinders X and Y each contain a sample of an ideal gas. The samples are in thermal equilibrium with each other.

X has a volume of 0.0260 m³ and contains 0.740 mol of gas at a pressure of 1.20 × 10⁵ Pa. Y has a volume of 0.0430 m³ and contains gas at a pressure of 2.90 × 10⁵ Pa. Data for the two cylinders are shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]
parts.text: Show that the temperature of the gas in X is 234 °C.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the number *N* of molecules of the gas in Y. Explain your reasoning.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The gas in X consists of molecules that each have a mass that is four times the mass of a molecule of the gas in Y.

Explain how the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) speed of the molecules in X compares with the r.m.s. speed of the molecules in Y.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: Two rectangular containers labeled X and Y show gas data: X contains 0.740 mol at 1.20 × 10⁵ Pa and has a volume of 0.0260 m³; Y is at 2.90 × 10⁵ Pa and has a volume of 0.0430 m³.
